tabs.description: Read URLs and titles of all open tabs
tabs.mv2_abuse: Full URL exfiltration: combined with webRequest gives complete browsing picture in real-time
tabs.mv3_abuse: URL/title still readable; exfil via fetch() to attacker domain remains viable; webRequest is now read-only

webRequest.description: Observe (and in MV2: modify/block) all HTTP/S requests
webRequest.mv2_abuse: Full MITM: block, redirect, or modify any request including auth headers and POST bodies
webRequest.mv3_abuse: Read-only in MV3 (blocking removed); can still log all request metadata and URLs

webRequestBlocking.description: Block or modify HTTP/S requests in-flight (MV2 only)
webRequestBlocking.mv2_abuse: Full MITM capability: inject code into any page response, strip CSP headers, redirect to phishing pages
webRequestBlocking.mv3_abuse: DOES NOT EXIST in MV3 - replaced by declarativeNetRequest

nativeMessaging.description: Communicate with native applications installed on the host OS
nativeMessaging.mv2_abuse: Full sandbox escape: talk to any registered host app, exfiltrate files, download payloads, achieve persistence beyond browser
nativeMessaging.mv3_abuse: Full sandbox escape: talk to any registered host app, exfiltrate files, download payloads, achieve persistence beyond browser — native messaging API is unchanged in MV3

debugger.description: Attach Chrome DevTools protocol to any tab
debugger.mv2_abuse: Full control of any tab: intercept network at protocol level, read all JS vars, inject code, capture screenshots silently
debugger.mv3_abuse: Identical in MV3 - debugger API is unchanged and provides full tab control

proxy.description: Control browser proxy settings, redirecting all traffic
proxy.mv2_abuse: Route all browser traffic through attacker-controlled proxy, full visibility into HTTP + HTTPS (if cert pinning absent)
proxy.mv3_abuse: Same in MV3 - proxy API is unchanged

cookies.description: Read and write cookies for any domain (when combined with host permissions)
cookies.mv2_abuse: Steal session cookies for any website the user visits, enabling account takeover without credentials
cookies.mv3_abuse: Steal session cookies for any website the user visits, enabling account takeover without credentials — cookies API is unchanged in MV3

history.mv2_abuse: Full browsing history exfiltration for user profiling, targeted phishing, or sale to data brokers

bookmarks.description: Read, create, modify, and delete bookmarks
bookmarks.mv2_abuse: Bookmarks reveal frequently visited sites, internal URLs (corp intranets), and saved credentials pages

storage.description: Read/write local and sync extension storage
storage.mv2_abuse: Persist stolen data locally; receive C2 configuration updates via chrome.storage.sync (syncs across devices)
storage.mv3_abuse: Same; storage.session added in MV3 (in-memory, not persisted) but local/sync unchanged

clipboardRead.description: Read clipboard contents without user gesture
clipboardRead.mv2_abuse: Steal 2FA codes, cryptocurrency wallet addresses, passwords copied to clipboard, or any sensitive text

clipboardWrite.description: Write to clipboard without user gesture
clipboardWrite.mv2_abuse: Replace clipboard content (e.g., swap crypto wallet addresses), inject malicious URLs

geolocation.mv2_abuse: Physical location tracking, builds movement profile

identity.description: Access OAuth2 tokens for Google or any configured provider
identity.mv2_abuse: Steal OAuth tokens to access user's Google account, Drive, Gmail, or third-party OAuth providers

webNavigation.description: Observe browser navigation events (URLs, timing, frames)
webNavigation.mv2_abuse: Silent real-time tracking of every page visited, including subframe loads (analytics, ads) with precise timing

scripting.description: Programmatically inject CSS and JavaScript into pages (MV3)
scripting.mv2_abuse: N/A - MV3 introduced scripting API; MV2 uses tabs.executeScript
scripting.mv3_abuse: Inject keyloggers, form stealers, or UI overlays into any page matching host_permissions. Combined with <all_urls>: universal code injection

activeTab.description: Temporary access to the currently active tab when user invokes the extension
activeTab.mv2_abuse: Limited: can execute JS in current tab only on explicit user action (click). Lower risk but still allows code injection
activeTab.mv3_abuse: Same constraint in MV3 - requires user gesture, restricted to one tab

downloads.description: Trigger file downloads and read download history
downloads.mv2_abuse: Download malware payloads to user's machine; exfiltrate data as files

notifications.mv2_abuse: Phishing via convincing system notifications; social engineering attacks

contextMenus.description: Add items to browser context (right-click) menus
contextMenus.mv2_abuse: Low risk alone; can capture selected text on context menu trigger

alarms.description: Schedule periodic callbacks (wake service worker on schedule)
alarms.mv2_abuse: Scheduled C2 check-ins, periodic data exfiltration without user interaction
alarms.mv3_abuse: Same but now primary mechanism for waking service workers - even more important in MV3 for C2 scheduling

offscreen.description: Create a hidden offscreen document for DOM manipulation (MV3 only)
offscreen.mv3_abuse: Hidden execution context outside service worker lifecycle; used to run code persistently, parse DOM, or execute side-channel operations invisible to users

declarativeNetRequest.description: Declaratively block or redirect network requests using static rules (MV3)
declarativeNetRequest.mv3_abuse: Static rules can include redirects to attacker domains; if rules are fetched dynamically from storage they can be updated without an extension update

declarativeNetRequestWithHostAccess.description: declarativeNetRequest with ability to redirect/modify requests to specific hosts
declarativeNetRequestWithHostAccess.mv3_abuse: Higher privilege than base declarativeNetRequest: can modify requests to matched hosts, enabling targeted MITM on specific sites

sidePanel.description: Display content in the browser side panel (MV3)
sidePanel.mv3_abuse: Persistent UI pane; can remain active and collect data longer than a popup; lower detection profile than background pages

<all_urls>.description: Access to all URLs - can inject content scripts or make requests to any site
<all_urls>.mv2_abuse: Universal content injection via content_scripts; access to every website's DOM, cookies (with cookies permission), and network traffic
<all_urls>.mv3_abuse: Same scope but injection now requires scripting permission too; host_permissions field in MV3 - still grants full-web access

management.description: List, enable, disable, or uninstall other extensions
management.mv2_abuse: Disable security extensions (ad blockers, password managers, AV extensions); silently install malicious extensions; enumerate all installed extensions for target selection
management.mv3_abuse: Disable security extensions (ad blockers, password managers, AV extensions); silently install malicious extensions; enumerate all installed extensions for target selection — management API is unchanged in MV3

contentSettings.description: Change browser content settings (camera, mic, geolocation, plugins per-site)
contentSettings.mv2_abuse: Enable camera/mic on malicious sites without user prompt

privacy.description: Read and modify Chrome privacy settings
privacy.mv2_abuse: Disable safe browsing, modify referrer settings, enable tracking protection bypass

unlimitedStorage.description: Remove the default 5MB storage quota — extension can store unlimited data locally
unlimitedStorage.mv2_abuse: Store arbitrarily large datasets locally — enables persistent exfiltration buffers, downloaded payloads, or offline C2 state without size constraints
unlimitedStorage.mv3_abuse: Same in MV3 — no quota means a compromised extension can cache gigabytes of stolen data or payloads on the victim machine

favicon.description: Access the favicon (site icon) for any URL without the user visiting it
favicon.mv2_abuse: Silently probe whether the user has visited specific URLs (banking, medical, political) by requesting their favicon — no network request visible to user. Reconstructs visit history without the history permission
favicon.mv3_abuse: Same in MV3 — favicon API unchanged. Combined with a known URL list, covertly maps visited sites

system.cpu.description: Read CPU architecture, core count, and processor details
system.cpu.mv2_abuse: Device fingerprinting — CPU info combined with other signals creates a near-unique device fingerprint for cross-session tracking. Also detects analysis sandboxes (single-core, slow CPU) to suppress malicious behaviour during review
system.cpu.mv3_abuse: Same in MV3 — sandbox evasion and fingerprinting vector unchanged

system.memory.description: Read total physical RAM on the device
system.memory.mv2_abuse: Device fingerprinting component — RAM size combined with CPU, screen, and timezone builds a highly unique device fingerprint. Also used to detect VMs and sandboxes (low RAM environments)
system.memory.mv3_abuse: Same in MV3 — sandbox evasion signal and fingerprinting vector unchanged

system.display.description: Read display configuration: resolution, color depth, DPI, orientation
system.display.mv2_abuse: Fingerprinting — screen resolution is one of the most distinctive browser fingerprint signals

system.storage.description: List available storage devices and their capacity
system.storage.mv2_abuse: Enumerate attached drives (USB, external) — fingerprinting and reconnaissance of connected storage media

system.powerSource.description: Read whether the device is on battery or AC power
system.powerSource.mv2_abuse: Sandbox evasion — analysis sandboxes run on AC power. Malware delays payload execution until battery mode is detected (real user device), evading automated review
system.powerSource.mv3_abuse: Same in MV3 — low risk alone but combined with system.cpu and system.memory forms a sandbox detection suite

processes.description: Access information about running browser processes and terminate them
processes.mv2_abuse: Enumerate all open tabs and frames as processes; terminate other tabs or the browser; identify which sites are open without the tabs permission
processes.mv3_abuse: Same in MV3 — rarely legitimate outside developer tooling

browsingData.description: Clear browser history, cookies, cache, passwords, and other stored data
browsingData.mv2_abuse: Destroy forensic evidence post-exfiltration — clear cookies, history, and saved passwords to cover tracks; also forces logout from all sites simultaneously
browsingData.mv3_abuse: Same in MV3 — browsingData API unchanged

topSites.description: Read the user's most frequently visited sites
topSites.mv2_abuse: Reveals highest-value targets (banking, email, healthcare) without full history access — enables precision phishing and user profiling

sessions.description: Access and restore recently closed tabs and windows across devices
sessions.mv2_abuse: Read recently closed tabs including post-closure URLs — stealthier than history permission, captures intent-sensitive browsing moments

windows.description: Query and manipulate browser windows (open, close, resize, focus)
windows.mv2_abuse: Open hidden popup windows for C2 communication or credential harvesting without user interaction
windows.mv3_abuse: Same in MV3 — combined with offscreen can create persistent invisible execution contexts

fontSettings.description: Read and modify per-script font substitution settings
fontSettings.mv2_abuse: Fingerprinting — installed font list is one of the most persistent browser fingerprint signals

userScripts.description: Register and execute arbitrary user scripts in page contexts (MV3 extension of scripting API)
userScripts.mv3_abuse: Inject arbitrary JavaScript into any page — functionally equivalent to remote code execution. Bypasses MV3 CSP restrictions that normally block eval(). Requires host_permissions but grants universal code injection once combined with <all_urls>

webAuthenticationProxy.description: Intercept WebAuthn (FIDO2/passkey) authentication requests and respond as a proxy
webAuthenticationProxy.mv3_abuse: Full MITM on hardware security key and passkey authentication — silently approve or deny WebAuthn challenges, intercept authentication tokens, or relay credentials to attacker infrastructure

vpnProvider.description: Implement a VPN client that controls all network traffic (Chrome OS only)
vpnProvider.mv2_abuse: Route ALL device network traffic through attacker-controlled infrastructure — complete network visibility on Chrome OS
vpnProvider.mv3_abuse: Same in MV3 — Chrome OS only but extremely high impact if present

platformKeys.description: Access platform-level X.509 certificates and sign data with platform keys
platformKeys.mv2_abuse: Sign arbitrary data using corporate or device certificates — impersonate the device in enterprise authentication systems, bypass certificate-based network access control
platformKeys.mv3_abuse: Same in MV3 — enterprise supply chain attack vector

certificateProvider.description: Act as a certificate provider for client TLS authentication
certificateProvider.mv2_abuse: Intercept or forge TLS client certificates in enterprise authentication flows; impersonate users in corporate SSO systems

gcm.description: Send and receive messages via Google Cloud Messaging / Firebase Cloud Messaging
gcm.mv2_abuse: Receive C2 commands via Google-controlled infrastructure — GCM traffic blends with legitimate push notifications and bypasses domain-based firewalls since it uses Google endpoints
gcm.mv3_abuse: Same in MV3 — GCM as a C2 channel is harder to block than direct attacker domains

input.description: Intercept and dispatch global keyboard and mouse input events (Chrome OS / kiosk mode)
input.mv2_abuse: Full keylogger capability at the OS input level — captures keystrokes globally including passwords typed outside the browser. Chrome OS / kiosk contexts only
input.mv3_abuse: Same in MV3 — available only in kiosk/Chrome OS contexts but extremely high impact on managed devices

readingList.description: Read and modify the browser Reading List
readingList.mv2_abuse: Reveals URLs the user saved for later reading — exposes interest areas and intent

fileBrowserHandler.description: Integrate with Chrome OS Files app to handle registered file types
fileBrowserHandler.mv2_abuse: Intercept file open events for registered types — silently read files the user opens in the Chrome OS Files app
fileBrowserHandler.mv3_abuse: Same in MV3 — Chrome OS only

fileSystemProvider.description: Mount a virtual filesystem accessible from the Chrome OS Files app
fileSystemProvider.mv2_abuse: Expose attacker-controlled content as local files to other apps; mount a persistent backdoor filesystem visible to users and other applications
fileSystemProvider.mv3_abuse: Same in MV3 — Chrome OS only but high impact on managed enterprise devices

tts.mv2_abuse: Low risk — social engineering potential via unexpected audio

ttsEngine.description: Implement a custom text-to-speech engine, intercepting all TTS requests
ttsEngine.mv2_abuse: Intercept and read all text-to-speech output from the browser and other extensions — passive audio eavesdropping

audio.mv2_abuse: Mute security audio warnings or manipulate user experience via audio state changes
